chapter_theme: Grace (அருளல்), the fifth of the Lord's five acts: the Lord who gladly made the worlds, the ages, the elements, the gods and the souls, and who binds and unbinds the body, stays near the mind of those who turn to him; he is in the body as milk is in water, and to see him there is bliss.
structure_note: The body tied and untied by the Lord (441), freedom from death for those who rejoice in nada (442), the potter's will (443), the Lord's eight qualities (444), three verses of repeated creation as gladness (445 to 447), his becoming the souls (448), and his presence as light and as milk in water, ending in the poet's own bliss (449, 450).

441.reading: The brow-eyed Lord sees to it: he ties and unties this bag of a body, which binds together the wind that blows in the eight directions, fire, the water of circling waves, the great earth and the sky, and is called the seat of life.
441.nuance: காயப்பை (the body as a bag) is plain, not contemptuous: the stress is on the Lord's tying and untying, birth and death, under a chapter on grace. வட்டத் திரை, circling waves, stands for water among the five elements.

442.reading: For those who long for the nada that rises and shines at the crown and take their joy in it, there is no Yama; he alone is able to fashion, as a carpenter does, the sky and the three spreading lights for the world.
442.nuance: உச்சியில் ஒளிதிகழ் நாதம், the shining sound at the crown, is a yogic term taken as the inner sound heard in meditation. விச்சும் is read as விசும்பு (sky), but may be வித்து (seed). The three lights are traditionally sun, moon and fire.

443.reading: From the clay set on his wheel the potter shapes whatever is in his mind; like the potter, if our lord Nandi wills it, the unmoving world becomes this or that.
443.nuance: The potter image makes the world the Lord's to shape at will. அசைவில் உலகம் (the world without motion) suggests inert matter that moves only by his will; the variant அயைவில் is unclear.

444.reading: He of wide expanse, the one unlike all others, the lord of a host of many bhutas, who by his nature has the bounty of keeping the world, whose qualities are the eight qualities, the matted-haired one, abides close to the mind.
444.nuance: எண்குணம், the eight qualities, is the term Kural 9 uses of the one to be worshipped. Here the eight belong to the matted-haired Siva. விரியுடையான் may mean the expansive one or the one with spread matted hair; விகிர்தன் is the one who is different, unlike the world.

445.reading: Gladly he made the seven worlds; gladly he made the many ages; gladly he made the five elements; gladly he made life and flesh.
445.nuance: உகந்து (gladly, delighting) opens every line. Placed under grace, the verse suggests that creation is itself an act of the Lord's goodwill toward souls, as tradition takes it: he makes bodies so that souls may work out their bonds.

446.reading: He made and owns the seven worlds of old; he made the many gods first; he made the many souls first; having made them, he stands as the Supreme.
446.nuance: படைத்துடையான் joins making and owning: he is maker and possessor. The verse repeats முன்னே (first, of old) for both gods and souls, so neither is prior to his making; it does not say whether souls themselves are created or only embodied, a point Siddhanta settles by holding souls to be beginningless.

447.reading: The First made the five great elements; the First made the many faultless ages; the First made the countless gods; and the First stands bearing all he made.
447.nuance: The last line adds keeping to making: தாங்கி நின்றான், he stands bearing them. The variant அனாதி (the beginningless) for ஆதி (the first) would sharpen the point that the maker has no beginning.

448.reading: He is vast, the seven wide realms becoming one in him; he is not easy to point to as 'this is he'; Siva himself becomes the many, many souls, and is the beloved one who spoke and came into the world.
448.nuance: சிவன்றான் பலபல சீவனும் ஆகி, Siva becoming the many souls, reads on its face as identity. Siddhanta tradition takes ஆகி as 'pervading as' or 'standing inseparably with', keeping Lord and soul distinct; the verse alone does not settle it. நவின்றான் (who spoke) is often taken as giving the Vedas and Agamas.

449.reading: The light within, the one body that stands close, the excellent thing the immortals in heaven desire, the one of holy form praised by the gods on earth, the great gem in the eye: this is the great awareness.
449.nuance: மண்ணின்ற வானோர், the gods who stand on earth, is usually taken as devotees or Brahmins. மாபோதம் (great awareness) and its variant மாபோதகம் (great teacher) give different endings: the Lord as knowledge itself, or as the teacher. கண்ணின்ற மாமணி may be the pupil of the eye, or a yogic light.

450.reading: I came to know the bliss of seeing, without slackening, how the holy form of the cosmos, which no one knows, stands rightly like milk in water within the vessel of the body, made from earth and the other elements.
450.nuance: கடம் (pot, vessel) is the body. Milk in water is a presence everywhere in it and inseparable from it, unseen but not absent; this answers 431, where the heart could not see the one within. The poet ends in the first person: he has found it.

links.note: Kural 9 calls the one to be worshipped எண்குணத்தான், possessor of eight qualities, without naming him; Tirumular gives the eight qualities to the matted-haired Siva who keeps the world and stays near the mind.
404 repeats ஒருவனுமே: one alone made, kept and removed the worlds. 445 to 447 use the same refrain form for creation, and 447 ends, like 404's second line, with his keeping what he made.

Both see the body as a pot. In the Naladiyar it is a woman's body, a pot oozing filth that fools admire for its skin; in Tirumular it is the vessel in which the Lord's form stands like milk in water, so to see within it is bliss.

Both use milk mixed in water. The Naladiyar's swan separates them, as the wise sort what is worth learning; Tirumular's milk stays in the water, the Lord present throughout the body and seen only by steady sight.

431, opening the chapter on concealment, says the heart lives with the Lord and does not know his form; 450, closing the chapter on grace, has the poet see that form standing in the body like milk in water.
Both turn to clay. In 440 one clay making many vessels shows one Lord behind many wombs; in 443 the potter shaping clay as he wishes shows the world becoming whatever Nandi wills.

source_issues: 442: விச்சும் is unclear; read as விசும்பு (sky), it may be வித்தும் (seed).
449: variant மாபோதகமே for மாபோதமாமே changes the ending from 'great awareness' to 'great teacher'.
